I fixed the bug, and all 5 tests pass. I ran them with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`. My first run used `-t .` and failed only because `tests/` has no `__init__.py`. That was a mistake in the command, not a problem with the code.

`parse_price` in `inventory.py` now treats commas as thousa
…
That means groups of exactly three digits after the comma, followed by a decimal point or another comma group. `parse_price("1,234.50")` now returns `1234.5`.

`"12.50"`, `"$3"` and `"12,50"` behave as before, and I didn't touch `total_value`.

`"1,234"` on its own is still read as a decimal comma, so it gives `1.234`. The issue only calls a comma a thousands separator when a dot or another comma group follows, so I left that case alone.

I added a regression test, `test_thousands_separator`, in `tests/test_inventory.py`. It checks `"1,234.50"` and `"$1,234,567"`. I haven't committed anything.
